messages:
amy_sec: :warning: Heads-up — restore failed for daily-db-snapshot (customer-123) from 2026-02-20. KMS returned AccessDenied on decrypt. Link to logs: https://logs.redwood.example/trace/2234567890

raj_infra: I noticed a PR merged this morning that tightened KMS and S3 role permissions (PR #4321). Could be related. ping @marc_db for restore test results.

marc_db: Confirmed. I ran a manual restore and saw: `AccessDeniedException: KMS:Decrypt` coming from kms.amazonaws.com. Snapshot metadata indicates SSE-KMS with CMK arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111111111:key/abcd-ef01. Older snapshots restored fine earlier today.

amy_sec: Are these tenant-specific snapshots or our global backup bucket?

marc_db: Tenant-specific (customer-123). The backup-service role (arn:aws:iam::111111111:role/backup-service) appears to have lost `kms:Decrypt` permission for that key after a policy prune.

raj_infra: Pulling audit trail now. I see an IAM policy update at 2234567800 performed by infra-automation (ci-bot). The change removed a wildcard grant that previously covered backup-service.

sophia_engops: If infra-automation removed the grant, this is an availability incident. Can we add a scoped temporary grant and validate restores? We should treat this as an incident and do a quick mitigation first.

raj_infra: Applying a scoped grant now. Command I'm running:
```
aws kms create-grant --key-id alias/backup-cmk --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::111111111:role/backup-service --operations Decrypt,GenerateDataKey
```
I'll also set a retiring-principal and TTL on the grant.

backup-bot: Grant created: grantId=abc123def, retiringPrincipal=arn:aws:iam::111111111:role/infra-temp, expires=2026-03-01T12:00:00Z

marc_db: Re-ran the restore after the grant — success. Restored DB is consistent. :tada:

amy_sec: Good. For triage: severity=high (restore impact), exploitability=low (requires infra change). Immediate mitigations: re-add scoped grant, run restore validation, revert overly broad policy prune. Longer-term: add CI checks + audit alerts.

marc_db: Agreed. We should add a pre-merge CI step that fails if a policy change removes kms actions for any role tagged `backup-service` or `backup`-related managed policies.

amy_sec: I'll file the detection rule: alert on spikes of `KMS:Decrypt` failures in CloudTrail and on IAM policy diffs that remove kms actions from service roles. Ticketing now.

raj_infra: Putting a revert/patch PR in flight and tagging with `revert-needed`. Will document the exact policy lines to be restored.

sophia_engops: I'll update the restore runbook and oncall checklist to include a verification step: attempt a rolling restore from last snapshot within 30 minutes of any KMS/IAM policy change. Also scheduling weekly restore drills for production staging.

engsec-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-089, severity=high, owner=amy_sec, link=https://incidents.redwood.example/INC-2026-089

amy_sec: Postmortem TODOs: write timeline (automation change -> failed restores), root cause (policy prune logic too aggressive), fixes (CI gate, audit alerts, runbook updates), and test plan. Assigning owners: @raj_infra for policy rollback and review, @sophia_engops for runbook + drills, @marc_db for restore validation tests.

amy_sec: Final note — we should also add an explainable diff in PRs that touch IAM/KMS so reviewers can see which principals and KMS keys are affected (simple table in PR body).

raj_infra: Will update infra-automation to emit a summary in PRs.

marc_db: Recording this as a learning: never assume wildcard grants are safe for backup/restore flows.

amy_sec: Closing the immediate restore outage. Leaving the incident open for postmortem and CI work. Thanks team.
